claim: Let \(J>0\) and \(h>0\), set \(k_B=1\), and consider two spin-1 qutrits with Hamiltonian \(H=-J(\mathbf S_1\cdot\mathbf S_2)^2+h(S_{1z}-S_{2z})\). Define \(T_{\mathrm{NPT}}(J,h)\) as the supremum of temperatures \(T>0\) for which the Gibbs state \(e^{-H/T}/\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-H/T})\) has a partial transpose that is not positive semidefinite. As \(h/J\to\infty\), \(T_{\mathrm{NPT}}(J,h)=\frac{2h}{\log(4h/J)+o(1)}\); equivalently, \(h/T_{\mathrm{NPT}}(J,h)=\frac12\log(4h/J)+o(1)\). The first loss of positivity is controlled by the partial-transpose block generated by the coherence between \(|1,-1\rangle\) and \(|-1,1\rangle\), rather than the two other off-diagonal blocks.

correctness.rationale: The spin-1 identity \((\mathbf S_1\cdot\mathbf S_2)^2=I+3P_0\) gives the exact 3x3 block. Partial transpose yields three explicit 2x2 blocks, so NPT is equivalent to the three stated inequalities. Perturbation of the lowest eigenpair gives \(g_{ac}=\frac{J}{4h}e^{2h/T}(1+o(1))\) in the threshold window; the other two block inequalities are asymptotically inactive there. The first crossing therefore has \(h/T=\frac12\log(4h/J)+o(1)\). The numerical script reproduces the first block crossing and is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The staggered field is a natural perturbation of the spin-1 biquadratic dimer, and the NPT threshold is a precise physically interpretable invariant. The result predicts NPT up to temperatures with \(T/J\to\infty\) while \(T/h\to0\), despite the strong field driving the ground state toward a product state. The exact coefficient and the identification of the responsible partial-transpose block distinguish this behavior from a generic numerical trend.
